headline.headline: PIRATES SILENCE PHILLIES, 6-1, IN CITIZENS BANK ROUT
headline.deck: Pittsburgh erupts for five unanswered runs after third inning to stun Philadelphia
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Pittsburgh Pirates arrived at Citizens Bank Park on Thursday as a team nobody in the National League wants to see in July, and they left with a resounding 6-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies before a crowd of 37,851 that grew quieter with every inning. The Pirates trailed by one after the Phillies scratched across a run in the third, then proceeded to score in five of the final six innings to leave no doubt.

Pittsburgh tied the game in the fifth and never looked back. Back-to-back crooked numbers in the seventh and eighth innings -- two runs and two more runs, respectively -- finished off the home side. Henry Gonzales clubbed his fourth homer of the season and Endy Rodriguez added his fifth, providing the power strokes that framed the offensive display. Alika Mangum, Ryan O'Hearn, Bryce Harper and Alec Bohm each collected doubles, while Bligh Madris contributed a triple. Josh Lowe added a stolen base as Pittsburgh kept the pressure relentless across three hours and two minutes of play.

Harper's double was one of the few bright spots for Philadelphia, which managed its lone run in the third inning and generated little else against a Pittsburgh pitching staff that locked down the Phillies lineup through the final six frames. The Pirates' ability to manufacture runs through a combination of power, extra-base hits and baserunning painted a picture of a team playing its sharpest baseball heading into the Independence Day holiday weekend.

secondary.headline: GUARDIANS WALK OFF WHITE SOX IN NINTH, 6-5
secondary.deck: Cleveland scores twice in the bottom of the ninth to deny Chicago on the road
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Cleveland Guardians needed every bit of the ninth inning to escape with a 6-5 win over the Chicago White Sox on Thursday, pushing across two runs in the bottom of the frame to erase a lead the visitors had held since the sixth. Chicago had battled back from a 2-0 deficit with three runs in the fifth and two more in the sixth to take a 5-3 edge into the late innings, and the Guardians needed a one-run seventh just to stay within striking distance.

Cleveland got the decisive rally in the ninth to finish off a game that featured wild pitching from both sides, with Martin and Cecconi each being charged with wild pitches in a chaotic outing. The White Sox, who were riding the momentum of that five-run swing across the fifth and sixth innings, could not hold the lead in front of an announced crowd of 22,556 at Progressive Field. The Guardians improved to claim the series advantage in what has been a scrappy early-July homestand.

secondary.headline: JA MORANT SHEDS NO. 12, STARTS FRESH IN PORTLAND WITH NO. 1
secondary.deck: Former Memphis star signals a new chapter by changing his jersey number with the Trail Blazers
secondary.body:
PORTLAND -- Ja Morant has worn No. 12 since his days at Crestwood High School in South Carolina, carried it through his college career at Murray State and made it synonymous with highlight-reel basketball in Memphis. Now, as he begins his tenure with the Portland Trail Blazers, the electrifying guard is making a clean break, switching to No. 1 as the franchise works to rebuild around him.

The number change is a small but pointed symbol of reinvention for one of the most gifted -- and scrutinized -- players in the league. Portland acquired Morant looking for a cornerstone talent to anchor a new era, and the guard appears eager to embrace that identity from the ground up. The Trail Blazers enter the 2026 offseason with Morant as the centerpiece of an ambitious retooling project, and No. 1 on his back sends a message about where his ambitions lie.

secondary.headline: WILD LAND COLEMAN, MAATTA IN BOLD OFFSEASON PUSH
secondary.deck: Minnesota adds proven forward and reliable defenseman from Calgary in a two-player trade
secondary.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- The Minnesota Wild wasted no time once the NHL calendar turned, acquiring veteran forward Blake Coleman and defenseman Olli Maatta from the Calgary Flames in a move that signals the organization's intention to compete immediately. Coleman brings a brand of physical, net-front hockey that head coach John Hynes has long valued, while Maatta provides steady blue-line depth that Minnesota identified as a priority heading into the new season.

The Wild had already been active in re-signing their own restricted and unrestricted free agents before turning to the trade market to add proven bodies. The NHL's free agency period opened June 30, and Minnesota has emerged as one of the more aggressive teams in reshaping its roster. The additions of Coleman and Maatta are expected to slide into complementary roles on a team that views itself as a legitimate Western Conference contender for 2026-27.

column.headline: THE PIRATES ARE NO JULY MIRAGE -- THIS TEAM CAN HURT YOU
column.body:
Six to one. In Philadelphia. With home runs, doubles, a triple and a stolen base scattered across the lineup. The Pittsburgh Pirates did not sneak past the Phillies on Thursday night -- they handled them, methodically, the way a team that believes in itself handles a club that expected an easy week at home. The Pirates trailed after three innings and scored in five of the last six. That is not luck. That is a baseball team that knows what it is doing.

The NL East is supposed to belong to the Phillies, the Braves, the Mets. Nobody put Pittsburgh on the July danger list, and that is precisely why the Pirates are dangerous. Henry Gonzales and Endy Rodriguez are hitting the ball out of the park. The pitching staff held Bryce Harper and Alec Bohm to a combined two doubles and nothing else of consequence. This franchise has spent years rebuilding, and the product on the field right now deserves more than a passing glance from the national baseball press. Watch the Pirates. They will not stop asking questions of the contenders around them.

story.headline: RAYS REEL OFF EIGHTH STRAIGHT, CARDINALS ERASE FIVE-RUN DEFICIT IN WILD THURSDAY SLATE
story.deck: Tampa Bay's winning streak reaches eight as St. Louis stuns Atlanta with seven-run seventh
story.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Cedric Mullins crushed a two-run homer and left-hander Ian Seymour baffled Kansas City hitters for the second time in seven days Thursday, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 5-2 victory over the Royals and their eighth consecutive win. Jensen and Collins also went deep for Tampa Bay, which scored three runs in the second inning and two more in the fifth to put the game away before 16,814 at Kauffman Stadium. The Rays, first in the AL East at 51-33, carry the streak into a Friday matchup with the Houston Astros.

In Atlanta, the St. Louis Cardinals trailed 5-3 after a wild first inning at Truist Park, then went silent for five innings before erupting for seven runs in the seventh to stun the Braves, 11-5, before 34,524 fans. Nolan Arenado and the Cardinals lineup roughed up Atlanta's bullpen in the decisive frame, with Burleson launching his 14th homer of the season, Jordan Walker adding his 19th, and Church connecting for his seventh. The Cardinals, who left 21 runners on base, improved to 45-39 and remain in contention in the NL Central.

Elsewhere around the majors, Pittsburgh's Gonzales and Rodriguez each homered as the Pirates quieted Philadelphia 6-1, with Pittsburgh scoring five of its six runs after the sixth inning. Colorado hammered Miami 14-4 at Coors Field, with a seven-run sixth inning doing most of the damage and McCarthy and Moniak going deep. Cleveland edged Chicago 6-5 on a two-run ninth, while Seattle blanked the Angels 1-0 on a single run in the sixth, with Ureña hitting both Arozarena and Robles in a tight pitching duel at T-Mobile Park.

story.headline: EASON STAYS IN HOUSTON AS ROCKETS LOCK UP RESTRICTED FREE AGENT ON FIVE-YEAR, $81.5M DEAL
story.deck: Tari Eason commits to Houston while Ja Morant debuts new number in Portland.
story.body:
The Houston Rockets secured one of the summer's most anticipated restricted free agent decisions Thursday, agreeing to keep Tari Eason on a five-year, $81.5 million contract, sources confirmed. The deal ends speculation that a rival team might submit an offer sheet the Rockets would be unwilling or unable to match, instead cementing the athletic forward as a cornerstone of Houston's young core alongside Alperen Sengun and Jalen Green.

Across the league, Ja Morant made his clean break from Memphis official in symbolic fashion, announcing he will wear No. 1 with the Portland Trail Blazers after sporting No. 12 throughout his entire career. Morant carried that number from Crestwood High School in South Carolina through his standout seasons at Murray State and into the NBA, making the switch a striking signal of the fresh start he is chasing in the Pacific Northwest after his turbulent final years with the Grizzlies.

Elsewhere around the association, veteran coach Billy Donovan agreed to join San Antonio as lead assistant under second-year head coach Mitch Johnson, a hire that brings two-time national championship pedigree to the Spurs bench as they develop Victor Wembanyama. The offseason also continued to generate debate among analysts grading the summer's biggest moves, with the Walker Kessler trade to the Los Angeles Lakers and extensions for Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili drawing heavy scrutiny from front offices and fans alike.

story.headline: OVECHKIN RETURNS FOR 22ND SEASON AS CAPITALS LOCK UP GOALS KING ON ONE-YEAR DEAL
story.deck: The 40-year-old legend is back in Washington, chasing history one more time.
story.body:
Alex Ovechkin, the greatest goal scorer in the history of professional hockey, will lace up his skates for a 22nd season in Washington after agreeing to a one-year contract with the Capitals, the team announced Friday. The 40-year-old Russian sniper, who shattered Wayne Gretzky's all-time NHL goals record during the 2024-25 season, returns to the only franchise he has ever known, giving Washington fans another chapter in the most prolific offensive career the sport has ever produced.

The signing sends a clear message across the league: Ovechkin is not finished adding to a total that already stands alone at the top of the record books. The left wing missed significant time in recent seasons due to injury but has repeatedly demonstrated the ability to find the back of the net with his trademark one-timer from the left circle, a shot that opposing goaltenders have failed to neutralize for more than two decades. General manager Brian MacLellan wasted little time locking up the franchise cornerstone as the free agency period opened.

The Ovechkin news overshadowed several other notable moves around the league, including the Minnesota Wild acquiring forward Blake Coleman and defenseman Olli Maatta from the Calgary Flames, bolstering a Minnesota roster that has long sought veteran playoff experience. Meanwhile, 18-year-old phenom Gavin McKenna expressed genuine enthusiasm about beginning his NHL career with the Toronto Maple Leafs, giving that storied franchise a potential cornerstone to build around for years to come.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Three franchises reshape their rosters with blockbuster moves at the game's most critical position.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into a full-blown quarterback frenzy, with franchises across the league making bold moves to secure the position that defines winning in the modern era. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a stunning trade this week, acquiring veteran signal-caller Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a package that included two second-round picks and a proven interior lineman. Raiders general manager Tom Telesco called the deal a cornerstone move heading into a rebuilding cycle that ownership demands produce results by year two.

Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers shocked the league by signing free agent quarterback Justin Fields to a three-year, $87 million contract, betting that a change of scenery and a new offensive coordinator can finally unlock the dual-threat weapon that scouts raved about coming out of Ohio State. Panthers head coach Dave Canales, who built a reputation for reviving struggling quarterbacks during his time in Seattle and Tampa Bay, met with Fields four times before the deal was struck. League sources say the Panthers structured the contract with significant performance incentives tied to completion percentage and playoff appearances.

The New Orleans Saints find themselves in the most uncertain position of any franchise, still weighing trade offers for veteran Derek Carr after a disappointing 2025 campaign in which the offense ranked 28th in scoring. Several teams, including the Tennessee Titans and the New York Giants, have expressed preliminary interest according to sources familiar with the conversations. The NFL draft in late April offered some teams quarterback solutions through rookies, but veterans with starting experience remain the hottest commodity on the market as minicamp invitations go out across all 32 cities.
